name: Cryptographic Implementation Review
description: Review of cryptographic implementations in source code for correctness and security. Covers identification of weak algorithms, insecure modes of operation, improper key management, IV/nonce reuse, padding oracle exposure, and misuse of cryptographic libraries.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to cryptographic implementation review

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands cryptographic primitives and common misuse patterns
evidence: Can explain symmetric vs. asymmetric encryption, hashing, and MAC
Familiar with deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA1, DES, RC4)
Understands the concept of cryptographic misuse vs. broken cryptography

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies obvious cryptographic misuse under supervision
evidence: Identified use of deprecated algorithms in code under guidance
Detected hardcoded keys and credentials in source code
Reviewed TLS configuration code for basic issues
Findings reviewed by authorized reviewer

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently reviews cryptographic implementations for common flaws
evidence: Independently reviewed cryptographic code on 5+ engagements
Identifies ECB mode, static IV/nonce, and insecure PRNG usage
Reviews key derivation functions and password hashing implementations
Evaluates certificate validation code for bypass vulnerabilities
Passed proficiency assessment on cryptographic review

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Reviews complex crypto implementations; identifies subtle timing and oracle issues
evidence: Identifies timing side-channels and padding oracle vulnerabilities in code
Reviews custom protocol implementations for cryptographic weaknesses
Evaluates key management lifecycles and secure storage mechanisms
Mentors others on cryptographic review methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on applied cryptography review; evaluates novel constructions
evidence: Published research on cryptographic implementation vulnerabilities
Reviews custom cryptographic protocols and novel constructions
Developed lab methodology for cryptographic implementation review
Trains teams on cryptographic code review

assessment_methods.description: Review a codebase with seeded cryptographic misuse (weak algorithms, IV reuse, hardcoded keys, timing leaks)
Given a custom authentication protocol implementation, identify cryptographic weaknesses
